common_name: Red Riding Hood Phlox (Compact Cherry-Red Garden Phlox)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in rich, moist, well-drained soil in full sun; this dwarf, compact selection suits containers and border fronts and benefits from good air circulation to limit powdery mildew.

directions: Red Riding Hood is a compact garden phlox reaching only about 18 inches tall, producing vivid clusters of fragrant cherry-red flowers on sturdy stems from midsummer into late summer. Its dwarf habit makes it well suited to containers and the front of the perennial border, unlike taller heirloom garden phlox that need to be sited toward the back. Grow it in full sun in fertile, consistently moist, well-drained soil, and avoid overhead watering to help minimize powdery mildew common to the species. The nectar-rich flowers draw hummingbirds and butterflies, and the cultivar has received the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit.

common_name: Speed Limit 45 Phlox (Chalky-Pink Rose-Eyed Garden Phlox)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun to part shade; this vigorous selection tolerates drier soil than most garden phlox once established.

directions: Speed Limit 45 is a vigorous garden phlox originally found growing wild along a North Carolina roadside, valued for its dense, fragrant flower clusters of soft chalky pink with a contrasting rose-red eye. Its fine-textured foliage carries reddish tints, and the plant is noted for excellent resistance to both powdery mildew and dry-soil conditions compared with many older garden phlox cultivars. It flowers over an unusually long season, from midsummer through early fall, in full sun to light part shade. Give it average, well-drained soil and moderate spacing for airflow, and it will thrive with less supplemental watering than most tall garden phlox.
sources: Chicago Botanic Garden Plant Evaluation Notes

common_name: Miss Elie Phlox (Red-Pink Mildew-Resistant Garden Phlox)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in fertile, evenly moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; good side-branching and mildew resistance make this a reliable border selection.

directions: Miss Elie bears large heads of red-pink flowers on well-branched stems from midsummer onward, and stood out in UK Royal Horticultural Society trials for its strong resistance to powdery mildew, a trait many older garden phlox lack. Its flowers also proved notably resistant to rain damage during trial evaluation, holding their form and color through wet summer weather better than many comparison cultivars. Grow it in fertile, evenly moist, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade, with adequate spacing between clumps to encourage airflow. Its dense, floriferous habit and clean foliage make it a dependable choice for mixed perennial borders.

common_name: Miss Pepper Phlox (Pale Pink Rose-Eyed Garden Phlox)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in fertile, evenly moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; dense flower heads benefit from good spacing and airflow to reduce powdery mildew.

directions: Miss Pepper is a remarkably floriferous garden phlox, its rounded flower heads densely crowded with small, pale baby-pink blooms, each centered with a concise deep rose-pink eye. The profusion of flowers gives the plant a softer, frothier look in the border than large-flowered garden phlox cultivars, and it continues blooming from summer into early fall. Site it in full sun to light part shade in fertile, evenly moist, well-drained soil, spacing clumps generously to promote air circulation and limit fungal leaf issues common to the species. It combines well with deeper-colored phlox and ornamental grasses as a softening element in mixed borders.

common_name: Younique Cerise Phlox (Compact Dark Pink Garden Phlox, Younique Series)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in fertile, evenly moist, well-drained soil in full sun; this compact, well-branched Dutch-bred selection suits smaller gardens and containers better than taller heirloom garden phlox.

directions: Younique Cerise is a dwarf, densely branched garden phlox from the Dutch-bred Younique series, producing rounded clusters of fragrant, vivid dark pink flowers on compact upright stems through summer. Its naturally reduced height compared with old-fashioned tall garden phlox makes it useful toward the front of the border or in large containers without staking. Grow it in full sun in fertile, evenly moist, well-drained soil, allowing enough space between plants for good airflow to help keep the narrow lance-shaped foliage free of powdery mildew. Regular deadheading of spent panicles encourages continued bloom into early fall.

common_name: Younique Mauve Phlox (Compact Soft Mauve White-Eyed Garden Phlox)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in fertile, evenly moist, well-drained soil in full sun; this compact Younique-series selection is well suited to smaller borders and mixed containers.

directions: Younique Mauve carries large clusters of soft mauve flowers, each marked with a bright white center, on a dwarf, compact plant that stays well branched without pinching. Like other members of the Younique series, it blooms earlier and more uniformly than many older tall garden phlox while remaining low enough to skip staking. Plant it in full sun in fertile, evenly moist, well-drained soil, with sufficient spacing around each clump to maintain airflow and reduce the powdery mildew that affects many summer phlox. Its gentle color pairs easily with deeper purples and blues in a mixed perennial planting.

common_name: Flame Coral Phlox (Dwarf Coral-Red Garden Phlox, Flame Series)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moderately fertile, medium-moisture, well-drained soil in full sun to very light shade; this naturally dwarf Flame-series selection needs no pinching to stay compact.

directions: Flame Coral is a naturally dwarf garden phlox from the Flame series, producing large clusters of fragrant coral-red flowers on upright, well-branched, compact stems that reach only about 12 to 18 inches. It flowers earlier in the season than many taller garden phlox and, with deadheading, will often rebloom into late summer. Its bushy, mildew-resistant habit and modest size make it a good fit for containers, courtyard gardens, and the middle of a smaller border. Grow it in full sun to very light shade in moderately fertile, evenly moist, well-drained soil, with enough spacing for airflow to keep foliage clean.

common_name: Super Ka-Pow White Phlox (Early-Blooming Compact White Garden Phlox)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in fertile, evenly moist, well-drained soil in full sun; this early-blooming, compact selection was bred for improved winter hardiness and powdery mildew resistance.

directions: Super Ka-Pow White is a compact garden phlox, roughly 18 inches tall, bred to open earlier in the season than standard tall garden phlox while carrying oversized, pure white flower heads on a well-branched frame. The series was developed for improved winter hardiness and better resistance to powdery mildew compared with older white-flowered cultivars, keeping its foliage cleaner through summer humidity. Grow it in full sun in fertile, evenly moist, well-drained soil, spacing plants to allow airflow around the dense flower clusters. Its early bloom extends the garden phlox season and pairs well with later-flowering perennials for continuous late-summer color.
